items.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first three-way summit
items.summary: The three leaders met for more than an hour in Shenzhen and issued a declaration on increasing oil supplies, reducing nuclear risks and reforming the U.N. The statement did not mention Russia's war in Ukraine or the U.S. war with Iran, and Poland's prime minister criticized Trump for calling Putin his friend.

items.headline: Trump says Iran war decisions can wait until new year
items.summary: President Trump said he is not rushing decisions on the nearly nine-month war with Iran, telling reporters "we've got time." The Republican-led Senate rejected a measure aimed at curbing the conflict.

items.headline: U.N. court rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
items.summary: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar's security forces acted with genocidal intent against the Rohingya during 2017 military operations in Rakhine state. Experts say the ruling is a landmark for international law.

items.headline: Democrats' midterm margin largest in 50 years
items.summary: Democrats won 56% of the national vote in House races to Republicans' 42%. The 14-point spread is the widest win for either party in half a century.

items.headline: U.S. loses measles elimination status
items.summary: The U.S., Mexico and Bolivia lost their measles-free status this week after prolonged outbreaks. Experts say most adults who had two doses of the MMR vaccine do not need a booster.

items.headline: Anthropic shares begin trading after record IPO
items.summary: Anthropic completed what is described as the largest IPO ever, valuing the AI company in the trillions of dollars. CEO Dario Amodei reiterated his commitment to developing AI responsibly.

items.headline: Judge extends block on Trump's triumphal arch
items.summary: A federal judge extended by 14 days an order barring the administration from breaking ground on a towering memorial arch in Washington. The order keeps construction on hold while the legal challenge continues.

items.headline: Three nations stall key U.N. climate report
items.summary: Russia, India and Saudi Arabia are holding up a major report from the U.N.'s climate science panel. Experts warn the political attacks could undermine the basis for future climate negotiations.

items.headline: FCC lets state prisons jam contraband phones
items.summary: The Federal Communications Commission voted to allow state prisons to jam signals from smuggled cellphones. Federal authorities view the devices as a major threat to prison security.

items.headline: Musk downplays support for Republicans
items.summary: Elon Musk played down his support for Republican candidates after record spending in the midterm elections. He said spending more than $400 million to back them was "pretty foolish."

digest.overview:
Democrats' midterm victory is now the largest for either party in 50 years, with the party winning 56% of the national House vote to Republicans' 42%. President Trump said major decisions on the nearly nine-month Iran war can wait until after the new year, and the Republican-led Senate rejected a measure to curb the conflict. Anthropic's shares began trading after what PBS NewsHour called the largest IPO ever. The U.S. lost its measles-elimination status, along with Mexico and Bolivia, after prolonged outbreaks. A federal judge extended by 14 days an order blocking construction of Trump's triumphal arch in Washington. The FCC voted to let state prisons jam signals from contraband cellphones. Trump also posthumously pardoned baseball's Pete Rose.

Abroad, Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held the first three-way meeting of their countries' leaders in Shenzhen, issuing a declaration on oil supplies, nuclear risks and U.N. reform that did not mention Ukraine or Iran. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk criticized Trump for calling Putin his friend, while European leaders meeting in Berlin pledged lasting support for Ukraine and Jared Kushner said the U.S. is open to an "Article 5-like" security guarantee for Kyiv. A Russian drone damaged the Dutch Embassy and a cathedral in Kyiv, killing at least one person. The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. In South Korea, the ruling Democratic Party moved to impeach Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, and Kakao founder Kim Beom-su was found not guilty in his second trial on stock manipulation charges. Experts warn that Russia, India and Saudi Arabia are stalling a key U.N. climate science report.

home.overview:
Houston rolled past Indianapolis 26–3 on Thursday night as C.J. Stroud threw three touchdown passes and Will Anderson Jr. added a safety, lifting the Texans to 4–6. The rest of Week 11 follows Sunday, headlined by Vikings–49ers in Mexico City, while the Rams' Puka Nacua drew a three-game suspension. In the NBA, the Knicks held off Minnesota 102–99 behind Karl-Anthony Towns' 22 and 12, Damian Lillard scored 33 in his Milwaukee return as Portland handed the Bucks a 12th straight loss, and Victor Wembanyama's 32 carried San Antonio past the Clippers. fact.answer:
Goosebumps happen when tiny muscles attached to each hair in your skin contract, pulling the hairs upright. The trigger is adrenaline, a stress hormone the body releases without our noticing when we feel cold or afraid.

In animals with thick fur, raising the hair traps a deeper layer of air that works as insulation, and it also makes a threatened animal, like a cat facing a dog, look bigger. Humans no longer have a hair coat, so the reaction does little for us, but it has stuck around.

That is why goosebumps also show up during strong emotions, such as at a wedding, hearing an anthem after a big win or watching a horror movie. They often come with other adrenaline signs, like tears, sweaty palms or a racing heart.
fact.question: Why do we get goosebumps?
